newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Grains-Focus on physical market.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Grains-Focus on physical market.

text.p: With Australian wheat futures trading lying near dormant this week, attention has been clearly centered on the physical market.
March wheat ended the week 50 cents lower at A$177.00 a tonne in week-long lacklustre trading conditions.

In contrast, Australia earlier this week was estimated to have made its way through about two-thirds of its 1996/97 export target of 17 million tonnes after selling 200,000 tonnes to India, raising the expectations of some that key Australian Wheat Board (AWB) pools may be closed soon.
The AWB on Monday closed 1996/97 pools for all grades of durum wheat, saying most supplies have been committed.

Expectations were lifted further following confirmation by the AWB on Friday that it had signed an agreement to sell at least 900,000 tonnes of wheat to Japan this year and held out the possibility the tonnage would climb to as high as 1.2 million.

Grains traders said initial deliveries were probably made at or near current AWB pool price estimates of A$193.00 a tonne for Australian Standard White (ASW) and A$206.00 a tonne for Australian Prime Hard (APH).

However, actual prices will be negotiated on a weekly tender basis, so the overall price of wheat to Japan will fluctuate throughout 1997 in line with international values, Nigel Officer, AWB manager of international sales said.
Of the minium tonnage to be bought, about 200,000 tonnes of APH wheat would be shipped from New South Wales and Queensland and 700,000 tonnes of ASW would be shipped from Western Australia.
"We would expect the prices achieved would be supportive of the pools," one trader said.
The agreement is expected to dampen some concerns that the number of internaional tender opportunities for Australia's bumper 23.5 million tonne crop this year was thinning.
Such sentiment followed comments by the AWB that opportunities for overseas sales were waning as buyers increasingly turn to domestic production.
With the Japanese business largely secured, the AWB is gearing up to aggreesively vie for a much-expected Pakistani tender for up to 270,000 tonnes of wheat for April delivery, traders said.

The latest sale to India brings Australia's total wheat sales to india this season to around 1.3 million tonnes, more than three-quarters of the total 1.7 million tonnes India is reported to have purchased this year, the AWB said.
